title: Building an LLM-powered DAG failure analysis plugin for Amazon MWAA
key_points: An Airflow plugin on MWAA sends a failed task's logs, DAG definition and the actual Glue or EMR script it ran to a Bedrock model and shows a root cause and fix in the Airflow UI.
Collecting operator-specific context (the real job code, not just the error) is what makes the answers specific.
Open-source sample with notes on prompt design, secret redaction and per-analysis cost.
services: Amazon MWAA, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR
decision: Manual log triage vs LLM-assisted root-cause analysis for pipeline failures
authors: Sushant Samantaray, Kamen Sharlandjiev, Parameswara Reddy Gajjela

title: Aurora PostgreSQL zero-ETL integration with Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Aurora PostgreSQL can now replicate continuously into a Glue managed catalog as Iceberg tables (backed by Redshift managed storage), queryable from Spark, SQL and BI tools without building a pipeline.
Explains the change data capture mechanics underneath and the setup steps: cluster parameters, target catalog, Lake Formation grants, authorising the integration.
Adds a lakehouse target alongside the existing Aurora-to-Redshift zero-ETL option.
services: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, zero-ETL integrations, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon Redshift, Apache Iceberg, Amazon SageMaker
decision: DMS CDC vs zero-ETL to Redshift vs zero-ETL to an Iceberg lakehouse catalog for Aurora PostgreSQL replication
attaches_to: aws-bytes: change data capture - DMS vs zero-ETL (later)
authors: Apurwa Pawar, Sarika Subramaniam

title: Announcing Spark Connect on Amazon EMR on EKS: Interactive PySpark development, anywhere
key_points: Spark Connect now also runs on EMR on EKS through a managed endpoint, letting local IDEs, notebooks and services drive Spark on a Kubernetes cluster.
Each session gets its own IAM role and cost tags; otherwise the same idea as the EMR on EC2 launch the same month.
services: Amazon EMR on EKS, Apache Spark, Spark Connect, Amazon EKS
authors: Amit Maindola, Al MS, Melody Yang

title: Getting started with Apache Iceberg write support in Amazon Redshift – Part 3
key_points: Redshift can now add, drop, rename and widen columns and change partitioning on Iceberg tables with ALTER, all as metadata changes with no rewrite of existing files.
Partition evolution covers adding, replacing and dropping fields and moving to multi-level partitions; old data keeps its old layout.
A Lake Formation resource link in the S3 Tables catalog lets Redshift query with two-part names and share the same tables with other engines under one permission model.
services: Amazon Redshift, Apache Iceberg, Amazon S3 Tables, AWS Lake Formation, AWS Glue Data Catalog
decision: Rewrite the table vs in-place schema and partition evolution when Iceberg tables written from Redshift change shape
authors: Raghu Kuppala, Sam Wang, Fahim Chowdhury, Tanishq Goyal, Sanket Hase, Vlad Ponomarenko

title: Enforce IAM permissions boundaries for Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio Tooling blueprints
key_points: SageMaker Unified Studio can now attach a custom permissions boundary to the IAM roles its Tooling blueprint creates, unblocking organisations whose SCPs demand boundaries on every role.
The example boundary blocks the AI agent actions; configured once via CLI and checked on a test project.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM, AWS Organizations SCPs
authors: Nexthink — Sanjana Sekar, Ganesh Sambandan, Luca Perrozzi, Paolo Romagnoli, Stefano Sandona

title: How Delivery Hero rebuilt real-time ad measurement with Apache Flink
key_points: Delivery Hero replaced hourly batch ad measurement with a five-stage Flink job: decrypt, deduplicate over a long window, enrich from DynamoDB with async lookups, join clicks to later orders, then aggregate.
Large keyed state in RocksDB carries both deduplication and the multi-day attribution join, and results are upserted to the reporting store every few minutes.
AWS reports delay fell from about an hour to about a second and running cost dropped by roughly 57 percent, with missing-session and timestamp gaps nearly eliminated.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon EventBridge Pipes, AWS Fargate, Amazon S3
decision: Hourly batch aggregation vs stateful stream processing for billing-grade event attribution
authors: Delivery Hero — Kirill Tishenkov, Alexandru Pisarenco, Francisco Morillo, Joseph Idicula Watasseril, Sabariesh Ganesan, Upendra Kambhampati

title: Query unstructured data in Amazon SageMaker Catalog using generative AI
key_points: Consumer half of a two-part series: find and subscribe to enriched documents in SageMaker Catalog, then ask questions about them through a no-code Bedrock chat agent or model calls from code.
Mostly console steps on top of the publish-subscribe flow.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon S3
authors: Nishchai JM, Aditya Edara, Narendra Gupta, Kiki Nwangwu

title: Configure domain-level VPC networking in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: A SageMaker Unified Studio domain can now hold one VPC setup that every new project inherits, instead of each project negotiating networking separately.
Existing projects without a VPC can adopt it; some must be recreated.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon VPC
authors: Prasad Nadig, Amit Shyam Jaisinghani, Arun Shanmugam

title: Announcing Spark Connect on Amazon EMR on EC2: Interactive PySpark anywhere
key_points: Spark Connect on EMR on EC2 lets PySpark run in a local IDE or a Unified Studio notebook while the cluster does the work, so you can set breakpoints against full-size data.
Each session is isolated with its own permissions, so a team can share one cluster instead of each running their own.
Ends the package-submit-wait loop and local-vs-cluster version drift.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache Spark, Spark Connect, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
decision: Cluster-bound notebooks vs submit-and-wait jobs vs Spark Connect from a local IDE for Spark development
authors: Al MS, Arun Prabakaran, Karthik Prabhakar, Rekha Veeraraghavan

title: How Moeve standardized dbt runs across data lakes with Amazon Athena
key_points: Moeve replaced team-by-team dbt setups with one launcher: Step Functions starts dbt in Fargate, run settings live in DynamoDB, and results are published to EventBridge for whatever orchestrates downstream.
Athena (with Iceberg for idempotent incremental loads) is the default engine, running in the account that owns the data through cross-account roles.
AWS reports onboarding a new dbt project dropped from days to about 15 minutes.
services: Amazon Athena, dbt, AWS Step Functions, AWS Fargate, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon EventBridge, Apache Iceberg
decision: Per-team dbt runners vs central config-driven dbt launcher decoupled from orchestration
authors: Moeve — Rubén Romero Córdoba, Álvaro Ponce Cabrera, Gonzalo Guerrero, Ricardo Bravo Panes

title: Best practices for scaling large consumer groups on Amazon MSK
key_points: A very large Kafka consumer group can produce a rebalance metadata record bigger than the default limit on the internal offsets topic, causing a loop of failed rebalances.
Fixes ranked: raise the size limit on that topic (with matching broker fetch settings), split the group, cut partition counts, and shorten member names; a sizing formula helps estimate the record.
The new consumer protocol in Kafka 4.0 (KIP-848) removes the problem at its root.
services: Amazon MSK, Apache Kafka, Amazon CloudWatch
decision: Raise offsets-topic size limit vs split consumer groups vs fewer partitions vs move to the KIP-848 protocol
authors: Pallavi Jha, Sunil Kumar Patro

title: Discover and govern Snowflake data using SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: Snowflake tables are federated into SageMaker Unified Studio through a Glue connection, so they can be queried and published to the catalog without copying them.
A Glue visual ETL job runs Glue Data Quality rules against the Snowflake data and posts the scores onto the catalog assets for consumers to see.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, AWS Glue Data Quality, AWS Glue, Snowflake
decision: Replicate external warehouse data to catalog it vs federate it and attach quality scores in place
attaches_to: aws-bytes: Data Quality Check (done) follow-up; governance (later)
authors: Marco Duarte, Diego Ortiz

title: How United Airlines uses Amazon Redshift and AWS Glue Data Catalog federation to query Databricks-managed data
key_points: United's curated gold tables sit on S3 but are catalogued in Databricks Unity Catalog, so Redshift could not see them without copying the data in and syncing it.
Glue Data Catalog federation reads Unity Catalog over the Iceberg REST API, Lake Formation vends credentials, and a resource link plus external schema lets Redshift Serverless query the tables live.
Removes duplicate storage and sync pipelines and turns Redshift into a pure query engine for analysts.
services: Amazon Redshift Serverless, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Lake Formation, Databricks Unity Catalog, Apache Iceberg
decision: Copy into Redshift managed storage vs federate the foreign catalog for cross-platform queries
authors: United Airlines — Vaibhav Agrawal, Ankit Aggarwal, Raja Kalluri

title: Connect Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio to Microsoft Power BI – Part 2: IAM-based domains
key_points: Same Power BI to SageMaker Unified Studio connection as Part 1, repeated for IAM-based domains.
Only differences are console paths, config values and an extra Identity Center permission set to hand out credentials.
services: Amazon Athena, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM Identity Center, Microsoft Power BI
authors: UC Irvine — Ramesh H Singh, Krishna Atluru, Armando Segnini, Saushthav Saxena, Gaurav Sharma

title: Connect Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio to Microsoft Power BI – Part 1: IAM Identity Center (IDC)-based domains
key_points: The Athena ODBC driver (2.2.0+) now signs in with SageMaker Unified Studio project credentials, so Power BI reaches governed catalog data directly instead of through a paid ODBC-JDBC bridge.

Two ways to connect: a DSN with the Athena Power BI connector, or DSN-less via the generic ODBC connector; publishing to Power BI Service needs the on-premises gateway on EC2 with its own IAM role added to the project.
UC Irvine is the customer example.
services: Amazon Athena, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS IAM Identity Center, Microsoft Power BI
decision: Third-party bridge vs native Athena ODBC auth (DSN vs DSN-less) for Power BI on governed AWS data
authors: UC Irvine — Ramesh H Singh, Krishna Atluru, Armando Segnini, Saushthav Saxena, Gaurav Sharma

title: Scale down Kinesis Data Streams on-demand capacity with ODA warm throughput
key_points: On-demand streams split shards during a spike but did not shrink afterwards; with On-demand Advantage you can now lower the warm throughput setting to give back capacity.
Fewer shards after a burst also means fewer parallel consumers to pay for downstream.
Covers which CloudWatch metrics and shard counts to watch while scaling down, and how much headroom to keep.
services: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon CloudWatch
decision: On-demand Standard vs On-demand Advantage with warm throughput vs provisioned shards for bursty streams
authors: Pratik Patel, Varsha Palepu, Priyanka Chaudhary

title: How to migrate from Amazon CloudSearch to Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
key_points: Step-by-step move from CloudSearch to an OpenSearch Serverless collection: map fields, re-ingest from the original source with OpenSearch Ingestion, convert queries, set security policies and validate before cutover.
CloudSearch has no export, so the source data must still exist elsewhere.
services: Amazon CloudSearch, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion
authors: Prasad Nadig, Jon Handler

title: Every team is a data team — bring Amazon Redshift analytics to ChatGPT Work
key_points: AWS released a plugin so the Data agent in ChatGPT Work can query Redshift (provisioned or Serverless) and lake data in plain language and turn answers into dashboards.
Users only see what their existing Redshift permissions allow, and existing cost and workload controls still apply.
Announcement only, no setup detail; signals that warehouse access by third-party agents is becoming normal.
services: Amazon Redshift, Amazon Redshift Serverless, ChatGPT Work
decision: BI dashboards vs AWS-native agents vs third-party chat agents as the self-service front end on the warehouse
authors: OpenAI — Naresh Chainani

title: Accelerating Spark queries with Iceberg materialized views
key_points: On EMR 7.12+ and Glue 5.1+, Spark can silently swap part of a query plan for a matching Iceberg materialized view in the Glue catalog, so slow dashboard or vendor SQL speeds up without being edited.

Compares three view designs for one query: broad pre-aggregates reused by many queries, narrower pre-joins, and an exact copy of one query; AWS reports about 5x, 10x and over 20x speedups on TPC-DS 3 TB.
Warns that rewrite adds planning time to every query and reading a small view can reduce parallelism.
services: Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Apache Iceberg, Apache Spark
decision: Broad reusable pre-aggregate vs narrow exact-match materialized view vs no view, when queries cannot be rewritten
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (Athena + Iceberg folder); aws-bytes: cost optimization (later)
authors: Yuzhou Sun, Henry Laih, Srikanth Kandula, Kinshuk Pahare, Shahryar Baki, Srishti Mittal

title: Build declarative ETL pipelines with AWS Glue 6.0
key_points: Glue 6.0 (Spark 4.1) adds Spark Declarative Pipelines: you declare bronze, silver and gold datasets in Python or SQL files and the framework works out order, checkpoints and retries inside one Glue job.
Removes the need for an Airflow or Step Functions DAG just to chain stages, and SQL and Python transforms can sit side by side.
Full CLI walkthrough with a dry-run validation step before the real run.
services: AWS Glue, Apache Spark, Amazon S3, AWS Glue Data Catalog
decision: Glue jobs chained by Step Functions vs Spark Declarative Pipelines vs Iceberg materialized views vs dbt for a medallion pipeline
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (NYC 311 medallion as the comparison dataset)
authors: Syed Humair, Bo Li, Kartik Panjabi, Shrey Malpani

title: How Sony LIV built real-time video streaming analytics with AWS
key_points: Sony LIV split viewer events into two paths: urgent signals (playback failures, live-sports engagement) go through Kinesis to ClickHouse for live dashboards, bulk events go through Firehose to S3 and Spark on EMR into Iceberg.
The Glue catalog ties both paths into one schema that feeds BI, ML features and future customer profiles.
Built for live cricket peaks such as the Asia Cup; a short story with no published figures beyond scale.
services: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon EMR, Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon EKS
decision: One batch path vs split hot path (stream to real-time store) and cold path (Firehose to Iceberg) for event analytics
authors: Sony LIV — Rahul Sureka, Umesh Chaudhari, Maheshwaran G, Varsha Palepu

title: AWS recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Strategic Cloud Platform Services for the 16th consecutive year
key_points: Gartner again names AWS a Leader for strategic cloud platform services.
The rest is a marketing summary of AWS's agent-ready data foundation message.
authors: Erika Ehrli

title: From silos to insights: Federated data access patterns for AI agents
key_points: One agent answers business questions across S3, Kinesis and a CRM database by calling MCP servers behind an AgentCore gateway, instead of first consolidating the data.
Three access patterns: catalog-first (discover via Glue Catalog, query via Athena), direct to the source system, and a hybrid of both.
The system prompt forces schema lookup before any SQL is written and routes questions by intent to the right tools.
services: Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Athena, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Model Context Protocol (MCP)
decision: Catalog-first vs direct source vs hybrid access for an agent answering questions across siloed systems
authors: James Wu, Anirudha Joshi, Amit Kalawat, Rahul Sharma

title: Network connectivity patterns for the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
key_points: The new OpenSearch Serverless uses ordinary PrivateLink endpoints with private DNS, so most private-access setups no longer need custom hosted zones or resolver endpoints.
Walks through nine patterns from one VPC to multi-account, on-premises and cross-Region.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, AWS PrivateLink, Amazon Route 53, AWS Transit Gateway
authors: Salman Ahmed, Ankush Goyal, Ravi Bhatane

title: How Moovit achieved 33% cost optimization through architectural modernization
key_points: Before moving anything, Moovit labelled every Redshift query by owner and workload type and ranked workloads by CPU time, then cut dead and over-scheduled jobs first.

Heavy raw-data aggregation moved to Spark on EMR after a PoC with pass/fail targets set up front, exploration moved to an isolated Redshift Serverless, and curated serving stayed on the provisioned cluster.
AWS reports the cluster shrank to half its size and overall pipeline cost fell 33 percent.
services: Amazon Redshift, Amazon Redshift Serverless, Amazon EMR, Amazon EMR Serverless, Amazon S3
decision: Keep scaling one Redshift cluster vs isolate workloads on Serverless vs offload heavy transforms to Spark
authors: Moovit — Saar Porat, Vova Nevski

title: Query Amazon S3 Tables from Amazon EMR Trino using the Iceberg REST endpoint
key_points: Trino on EMR can read and write S3 Tables through the standard Iceberg REST catalog endpoint, so table maintenance stays managed while Trino does the SQL.
Mostly a CloudFormation setup walkthrough; the takeaway is that the REST catalog lets any compliant engine join the same tables.
services: Amazon EMR, Trino, Amazon S3 Tables, Apache Iceberg
decision: Engine-specific catalog integration vs Iceberg REST endpoint for multi-engine access to S3 Tables
authors: Shubham Purwar, Anirudh Chawla, Nitin Kumar, Prashanthi Chinthala

title: Building medallion architecture with Iceberg materialized views in Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Each medallion layer becomes one SQL materialized view over Iceberg (S3 Tables), and the catalog's managed Spark refreshes it incrementally, replacing separate ETL jobs, orchestrator DAGs and hand-written change detection.

The limits are the real story: refresh at most hourly, Gold does not refresh automatically after Silver, deletes need a full refresh, schema changes mean drop and recreate, and the feature is AWS-only.
AWS reports scheduled refresh is billed per DPU-hour of managed Spark, with view data charged as normal S3 storage.
services: Apache Iceberg, Amazon S3 Tables, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Glue, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
decision: dbt models vs orchestrated Glue jobs vs Iceberg materialized views for a bronze-silver-gold lakehouse
authors: Gaurav Sharma, Matt David

title: Build a dynamic streaming data lake with Apache Iceberg and Apache Flink
key_points: Iceberg's dynamic sink for Flink routes each record to the right table and adds new columns as they show up, so a new event type or field no longer forces a stop-edit-redeploy of the job.
Two ways to know the schema: infer it from each JSON record, or look it up in a schema registry; a list of candidate partition columns keeps new tables partitioned sensibly.
Built on Managed Service for Apache Flink reading from Kinesis, with sample code on GitHub.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Glue Schema Registry
decision: Fixed per-table sinks with redeploy on schema change vs dynamic sink with per-record routing and automatic schema evolution
authors: Francisco Morillo, Felix John

title: Observing and evaluating production agents using OpenSearch Agent Health
key_points: AI agents emit OpenTelemetry traces into OpenSearch Ingestion and OpenSearch Service; the open-source Agent Health tool, run locally, inspects those traces and runs evaluation test cases.
Pitches observability plus evals as the agent equivalent of unit and integration tests, usable as quality gates.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion, OpenTelemetry
authors: Ulrich Hinze, Megha Goyal, Rekha Thottan

title: Accelerate Apache Spark debugging on Amazon EMR with AWS DevOps Agent
key_points: The generic DevOps Agent can see that a Spark executor died but not why; plugging in AWS's managed Spark troubleshooting MCP server lets it read event logs, executor memory and the offending code line.
The MCP server is registered as a custom capability over PrivateLink, and the demo goes from a CloudWatch alarm on a failing EMR job to a root cause and suggested fix in one chat.
Shows the general pattern of extending an ops agent with service-specific MCP tools.
services: Amazon EMR, AWS DevOps Agent, Apache Spark, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Amazon CloudWatch, AWS PrivateLink
decision: Manual log digging vs generic ops agent vs ops agent extended with Spark-aware MCP tools for Spark failure root cause
authors: Kalyan Janaki, Aneesh Varghese
